dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether the logic for calculating the delivery fee accurately applies the student's defined rules for all valid inputs and produces the expected final fee.
sub_criteria: The base fee (if defined) is correctly applied to the initial fee.
The logic for distance-based fee adjustments correctly calculates and adds the corresponding amount.
The logic for order value-based fee adjustments (e.g., surcharges, discounts) correctly modifies the fee based on defined thresholds.
All individual fee components are correctly combined to produce the final delivery fee.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: Assesses if all necessary components for a delivery fee calculation, including inputs, outputs, and conditional logic, are present and adequately addressed.
sub_criteria: The algorithm accepts order value and delivery distance as inputs.
The algorithm defines at least two distinct factors or rules that influence the delivery fee (e.g., a base fee, a distance rate, an order value threshold).
Conditional logic is present to apply different fee adjustments based on input values (e.g., if distance is X, if order value is Y).
The algorithm includes handling for common edge cases, such as a zero or very small order value, or a zero distance.
The algorithm produces a final calculated delivery fee as output.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: Examines how easily a human can understand the pseudocode's steps, variable usage, and overall logical flow without ambiguity.
sub_criteria: Variable names are meaningful and clearly represent the data they hold (e.g., 'orderValue', 'deliveryDistance', 'finalFee').
Each step of the calculation and decision-making process is described in clear, easy-to-understand language.
The logical flow from input to final output is straightforward and easy to trace.
References to values or intermediate results are unambiguous throughout the pseudocode.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether the algorithm avoids redundant calculations or unnecessary logical checks, reflecting an awareness of computational performance.
sub_criteria: The algorithm calculates each fee component only once without unnecessary repetition.
The pseudocode avoids redundant conditional checks that could be combined or nested more effectively.
